chapter: First bands, Ennis, Thornhill and the Army
title: Members of the first Stockton band
summary: Gil names the players of his first band, including Ned Briggs, Herb Stowe and C. L. McPherson, as Johnston asks.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Are some of them, do you know whether most of them are still living now or not?
The bass player is the man I met in the Hawaiian Islands.
Yes, yes. What was his name?
Uhu. Can you remember off-hand the names of the men in that first band that you organised right after highschool?
Alright, would you give them to me, and the instruments they played?
They're not working as musicians any more.
No, but I'm interested in the makeup of your first orchestra.
Well, Ralph Liscombe was the trumpet player.
Ned Briggs brother, Clark Briggs was another trumpet player.
Would you speak up just a little bit at the microphone.
Louis Cazalé was another trumpet player. Cazale really, but we pronounced it Cazalé.
Would you spell that one for me, I'm not even going to try that. (LAUGHTER).

The trombone player was a man named Norris Hurley Hal Sloane, the drummers were Norman Sloane and Don De. Soto and a fellow named Leroy Judd. And the saxophone, Herb Stowe (Burt Stowe?). He was the grandson of Harriet Beecher Stowe.
Have you ever known his grandmother?
His Mama. As a matter of fact, what was, Al, I can't think of very good player, Al's last name, very diplomatic. C. L. McPherson.
